mappings.note: Share of the world's people engaged in agriculture. Not a crop, farming type or practice (LO-12), nor a country's crop specialism (LO-13); the competency is the nearest code for a framing statistic about agriculture.
Agriculture as a primary activity. The primary/secondary/tertiary triad has no outcome anywhere in curriculum 130; cited to the agriculture competency because agriculture is the subject of the item.
Proportion of India's population dependent on agriculture -> LO-12, the outcome about agriculture in one's own country, rather than LO-14, since no farming type is being related to development.
Definition of arable land; terminology rather than a described crop or practice -> competency.
Jhumming located in north-eastern India is an agricultural practice in one's own country -> LO-12 exactly.
Which animal belongs to a nomadic herd; a detail of the nomadic herding practice -> LO-12, not LO-14, which is about farming and development.
Physical inputs to agriculture; the farm-system input list is terminology and has no LO -> competency.
Another farming-input item -> competency, same gap.
Viticulture defined; terminology -> competency.

Example of a tertiary activity. The item names services rather than farming, so it sits on the industry side; C-SST2.1 classifies industries, which is the nearest classification code, and the primary/secondary/tertiary gap is noted.
Fishing as a primary activity; classification of an agriculture-family activity -> competency, same gap as qid:110233.
Latin origin of the word agriculture; etymology -> competency.
Floriculture named; terminology -> competency.
Seeds as an input to agriculture -> competency, the farm-system input gap.
Local name for shifting cultivation in Malaysia; a named type of farming -> LO-12. Not LO-13, which is about countries known for producing wheat, rice, cotton or jute.
Local name for shifting cultivation in Mexico -> LO-12, same reasoning.
Local name for shifting cultivation in Brazil -> LO-12.
Which country practises Roca; the item is about the farming practice, not about crop production leadership -> LO-12.
Indian states where nomadic herding is practised -> LO-12, a farming practice in one's own country.
Sericulture named; terminology -> competency.
Crop grown extensively in the USA -> LO-13, which is about countries known for producing particular crops.
Season in which wheat is grown in India -> LO-12, a crop practice in one's own country.
Extraction of natural resources classified as primary activity -> competency, the economic-activity gap.
Which regions favour agriculture is a question about the factors behind crop production -> LO-13, not LO-12's description of practices.
Important input of farming -> competency, input-list gap.
Definition of agriculture as the art and science of soil cultivation -> competency.
Conditions under which shifting cultivation is practised; a characteristic of the farming type -> LO-12.
Nomadic herding in the Sahara; the farming type in a named region -> LO-12.
A crop grown under commercial farming; the answer is a crop, so LO-12 rather than LO-14, which is for relating the farming type to development.
Where mixed farming is practised -> LO-12, a farming type placed geographically.
A tropical plantation crop -> LO-12.
Which crop constitutes a plantation -> LO-12.
Pisciculture named; terminology -> competency.
Which activities are primary -> competency, the economic-activity gap.
Seeds, fertilisers and machinery as the inputs of the farm system -> competency.
Farming to meet family needs is subsistence farming; naming the type by its economic purpose is the farming-and-development link -> LO-14, not LO-12's description of practices.
Sub-types of subsistence farming (intensive and primitive) -> LO-14, the same classification by economic character.
Which option is not commercial farming; the subsistence/commercial distinction -> LO-14.
Paddy identified as rice; a major crop -> LO-12.
Which crops commercial grain farming raises; the answer is a crop list -> LO-12, with LO-14 reserved for items that turn on the farming type's economics.
Identifying coarse grains; crop classification -> LO-12.
Leading rice-producing country -> LO-13, which names rice explicitly.
Soil suited to wheat is one of the factors behind wheat production -> LO-13, which names wheat.
The fibre needing frost-free days is cotton; a growing-condition factor for a crop LO-13 names.
Naming the types of economic activity -> competency, the primary/secondary/tertiary gap.
Literal meaning of 'agri'; etymology -> competency.
Profit motive, large area, capital and technology identify commercial farming; characterising a farming type by its economic footing -> LO-14.
Example of a secondary economic activity, i.e. manufacturing; the industry side, so the industry-classification competency, with the same triad gap noted.
Jute as the Golden Fibre; recall of a major crop's name rather than of the factors behind its production -> LO-12, not LO-13.
